judgements.justification: B's chair did not argue acceptance against eiQW's 4; it ignored the 4, called the reviews 'overwhelmingly positive', and the 6.0 mean, not a defence of acceptance, set the poster.
The authors posted no new experiments on either forum; A got only promised kNN, EDGE and MINE comparisons.
No high-confidence expert rated above lower-confidence peers; B's highest-confidence reviewer, eiQW (4), gave the lowest score.
CzLh and 6PJ4 added the DPI concern after the rebuttal but changed no score, and the authors had already conceded the point.
B's lower ratings matched real conceded errors and eiQW's critique, so the gap reflects different judgements, not leniency on equal assessments.

B judged the 'no curse of dimensionality' and DPI-violation-as-advantage claims overstated and its chair made fixing the DPI framing the condition of acceptance, while A took both claims at face value.
Neither committee's reviewers converged on flat marginal scores; A rated 6, 7, 7, 8 and B 4, 7, 6, 7.
